subject: Life Skills
title: Poisoning Prevention at Home
description: A short lesson to help you apply Poisoning Prevention at Home.

hook.text: Poison control centers in the US handle 2.1 million calls per year. Most involve everyday household products.

buildup.text: Cleaning agents, medications, and even certain plants are the top culprits. Children under five are the most at risk.

discovery.text: Store chemicals in original labeled containers. Never transfer bleach into a water bottle — it has killed people.

twist.text: Mixing bleach with ammonia creates toxic chloramine gas. Many common cleaners contain ammonia. Read labels every time.

climax.text: Save your local poison control number in your phone now. Fast advice in the first minutes makes the biggest difference.

punchline.text: Label it, lock it, never mix it. Simple saves lives.
